parameters.description: The partition type or identifier. The byte limitation indicates that a given partition format can only support 256 different partition types. There is not one to one correspondence between this identifier and the types of file systems supported. In actuality the number of file systems is less because multiple partition types might map to the same file system, and some partition types might have no file system associated with them but indicate something specific. Partition type Description PART_UNKNOWN Partition type is unknown. PART_DOS2_FAT Legitimate DOS partition. PART_DOS3_FAT Legitimate DOS partition. PART_DOS4_FAT Legitimate DOS partition. PART_DOS32 Legitimate DOS partition (FAT32). P

documented_values.description: Partition type is invalid or not used.

parameters.name: bPartType

parameters.description: This is a 64-bit number indicating the size of the partition to create. A partition driver is not required to support the full 64 bits.
parameters.name: numSectors

parameters.description: When this flag is set, bPartType is ignored and the partition driver is allowed to generate the appropriate partition type for the default file system type that it supports. In the case of FAT, it will select a partition type based on the number of sectors in this partition, FAT12, FAT16 or FAT32.

declaration: DWORD PD_DeviceIoControl(DWORD dwPartitionId, DWORD dwCode, PBYTE pInBuf, DWORD nInBufSize, PBYTE pOutBuf, DWORD nOutBufSize, PDWORD pBytesReturned);

evidence.detail: declaration, requirements block, parameter list read mechanically from the page

parameters.description: Handle to the device that is to perform the operation. Call the CreateFile function to obtain a device handle.
parameters.name: dwPartitionId

parameters.description: Specifies the control code for the operation. This value identifies the specific operation to be performed and the type of device on which the operation is to be performed. The writer of a custom device driver can define IOCTLs with the CTL_CODE macro. These control codes can then be advertised, and an application can use these control codes with DeviceIoControl to perform the driver-specific functions.
parameters.name: dwCode

parameters.description: Long pointer to a buffer that contains the data required to perform the operation. This parameter can be NULL if the dwIoControlCode parameter specifies an operation that does not require input data.
parameters.name: pInBuf

parameters.description: Size, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by lpInBuffer .
parameters.name: nInBufSize

parameters.description: Long pointer to a buffer that receives the operation's output data. This parameter can be NULL if the dwIoControlCode parameter specifies an operation that does not produce output data.
parameters.name: pOutBuf

parameters.description: Size, in bytes, of the buffer pointed to by lpOutBuffer .
parameters.name: nOutBufSize

parameters.description: Long pointer to a variable that receives the size, in bytes, of the data stored into the buffer pointed to by lpOutBuffer . The lpBytesReturned parameter cannot be NULL. Even when an operation produces no output data, and lpOutBuffer can be NULL, the DeviceIoControl function makes use of the variable pointed to by lpBytesReturned . After such an operation, the value of the variable is without meaning.
parameters.name: pBytesReturned
